messages.author: fa51e47cdd090afc
messages.subject: Delete calibrating masses from analysis
parts:
Hi all,
i've a question. I'm analyzing some datasets where i'm using trypsin(842.508), angioII(1046.19) and glufib(1570.67) as internal calibrants when i scan the tissues. 
I wonder if there is any way to delete them from the datasets just to avoid false positives or misleading predicting peaks.
Thanks in advance
Edu

messages.author: fa6884457716c3bb
messages.subject: Re: Delete calibrating masses from analysis
parts:
You can use negative indexing as shown below. note this example works for peak data, not full mass range data.

#the features function will return the indices for an m/z or list of m/zs 
calibrant_masses <- features(cardinaldata, mz=c(842.508, 1046.191,570.67))

#print dataset info
summary(cardinaldata)

Class: MSImageSet
Features: m/z = 501.26 ... m/z = 992.7 (344 total)

#the MSImageSet is organized msset[features, pixels]
#use negative index to remove features, shown below:

cardinaldata <- cardinaldata[-calibrant_masses,]

summary(cardinaldata)

Class: MSImageSet
Features: m/z = 501.26 ... m/z = 986.7 (341 total)

Alternatively, as a one-liner:
cardinaldata <- cardinaldata[-features(cardinaldata, mz=c(842.508, 1046.191,570.67)),]

a forewarning with picked peak data, check the ion images and line plots of the picked peak data at the masses of your calibrants a to ensure you are removing the calibrants and not an adjacent peak. The peak picking and alignment oftentimes will shift the mass of the peaks from the value you see in individual spectra. The features function will find the peak with the closet value to what you input in mz, so if there is significant shift, it may detect an adjacent peak rather than your calibrant.

Best of luck,
Heath
